problem: The figure labels four implanted piezoresistors with ΔR/R = 0.024 and says the bridge hands 0.03 V to the amplifier and ADC. With all four gauges active the bridge output is V_s·(ΔR/R) = 5 V × 0.024 = 0.12 V. 0.03 V is the one-active-gauge value from worked example 1, so the figure contradicts the example and the text, and would push a student into the exact error listed in exam trap 1.
fix: Either change the bridge node to '0.12 V out' (and the caption to '... form a bridge that hands 0.12 V to the amplifier and ADC'), or keep 0.03 V and label the resistor node 'one active gauge, ΔR/R = 0.024'.

problem: 'the difference voltage is proportional to mass flow' is wrong. The differential-thermopile (calorimetric) output rises roughly linearly only at very small flow and then follows a strongly nonlinear, saturating curve (hot-wire anemometers follow King's law, output ≈ a + b·(mass flow)^0.5). A student writing 'proportional' loses marks and cannot explain the calibration curve.
fix: 'the difference voltage rises with mass flow but not linearly: it is close to linear at very low flow and flattens at higher flow, so the part is calibrated with a look-up table; the sign of the difference gives the direction.'

problem: 'commercial parts run from about 5 to 20 mV/V' drops the 'per bar' basis, so it cannot be compared with the 6 mV/V/bar just quoted or with data sheets.
fix: 'commercial parts run from about 5 to 20 mV/V/bar at full-scale pressure.'
